source_title: Trade Corridors Matter More Than Ideology
summary: This September 2025 interview gives Prediction As Falsifiable Prophecy an earlier public method statement, then turns the Tianjin/SCO summit into dated forecast pressure around trade corridors, payment rails, Iran/Hormuz, U.S.-China rapprochement, and Taiwan non-invasion.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Treat this as an earlier public Predictive History method statement before the 2026 hostile-audit and final-exam sources: history should connect the past, explain the present, predict the future, and let predictions validate or break the model.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Prediction owns this method pressure because Jiang makes model validation depend on future-facing claims. Living School owns the pedagogical version only when the active mechanism is classroom practice, student questioning, or formation.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use this source as pre-Iran-war corridor evidence: Jiang says the coming U.S.-China conflict turns on trade networks, SWIFT alternatives, petrodollar dependence, Iran's position in Belt and Road and the North-South Corridor, Hormuz, and East Asian energy exposure.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Chokepoint owns this when the active board is routes, energy, payment rails, and access. Prediction owns the five-to-ten-year horizon and later comparison; Power As Alchemy owns dollar and sanctions when monetary reality is primary.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold this source for a Power pass on financial sovereignty after sanctions: frozen Russian assets and SWIFT exclusion become proof that Western financial assets can be politically seized, creating an opening for Chinese-led banks, payment rails, and a currency-basket alternative that supplements rather than instantly replaces the dollar.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Power As Alchemy gets the monetary-belief and asset-sovereignty layer. Chokepoint gets the same material only when the payment system is tied to route control, energy access, or war exits.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Keep Jiang's 'no clear lines' rule as a Game Theory support point: alliance maps mislead because each player maximizes options, preserves flexibility, and may develop stronger long-term tension with a neighbor than with an apparent ideological enemy.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Game Theory owns the option-preserving player map. Chokepoint owns the same relations only when the material route or energy board is the active mechanism.

chronology_notes.note: This September 1, 2025 source predates the January 2026 grand-bargain interview and the March-April Iran-war cluster, so it should be treated as earlier corridor-order and Predictive History method pressure rather than a late explanation of those later claims.

The source gives an early version of China as trade-and-consensus power versus America as ideological hegemony, but Jiang qualifies the contrast by saying any country controlling institutions will use them for national interests and that China's newcomer position forces consensus-building.

The Taiwan claim is a dated 2025-09-01 forecast and public-discourse diagnosis, not a timeless principle: Jiang says China will not invade Taiwan, offers a million-dollar bet, and grounds the claim partly in what he says people in China and Taiwan are actually discussing.

canon_candidates.candidate: In the next five to ten years, the main U.S.-China conflict will center on trade corridors, alternatives to SWIFT, petrodollar dependence, and Middle Eastern route security rather than ideology alone.
canon_candidates.promotion_condition: Compare with the 2026 Chokepoint sources before promotion; keep the horizon and corridor/payment-rail mechanism distinct from later Iran-war escalation claims.

canon_candidates.candidate: China will not send ground troops to the Middle East and will instead try to mediate or facilitate peace if a U.S.-Iran war breaks out, while Russia is more likely to protect Iran.
canon_candidates.promotion_condition: Compare with later March-April Iran-war sources and preserve the conditional structure around a U.S.-Iran war.

canon_candidates.candidate: Within six months, China and the United States will reach a behind-the-scenes compromise that publicly looks like a Chinese win while helping stabilize the dollar and reduce U.S. debt pressure.
canon_candidates.promotion_condition: Compare with the January 5 grand-bargain interview and the May 2026 bargain/theater sources before any ledger item; preserve the six-month and half-year-to-one-year horizons.

canon_candidates.candidate: China will not invade Taiwan, and invasion talk functions more as a Pentagon funding narrative than as a live Chinese policy agenda.
canon_candidates.promotion_condition: Compare with later Taiwan and U.S.-China bargain sources; keep Jiang's public-discourse evidence separate from the categorical forecast.

next_actions.action: Do not append ordinary prose to Chokepoint from this source yet. The useful next step is a Prediction-side comparison queue that connects this September 2025 corridor/payment-rail forecast to the January grand-bargain and March-April Chokepoint sources.

If a public Prediction mutation follows, add only a compact chronology note or lens-point strengthening for the earlier method statement; avoid creating a separate Tianjin summit, SCO, Taiwan, or China soft-power page.

When comparing forecast candidates, separate four families: corridor/payment-rail five-to-ten-year structure, China no-ground-troops mediation claim, U.S.-China six-month compromise, and Taiwan non-invasion. They have different test windows and should not be collapsed into one China-rise ledger item.
